newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Australia's Colonial may raise capital at listing.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Colonial may raise capital at listing.

text.p: Australia's Colonial Mutual Group may seek to raise some capital as part of its planned demutualisation and stock market listing, chief executive and managing director Peter Smedley said on Friday.
"We will probably be looking at capital raising of some kind," Smedley told reporters in Hong Kong, but he declined to say how much might be sought.

Capital raising could be through the placement of new shares, the purchasing of shares from policy holders who did not want them which could then be placed elsewhere, or a combination of some kind, he said.
Any plan would be announced at the group's planned meeting of policy holders in November, pending Australian court approval of the demutualisation plan, he added.
Colonial said in July it would not offer a cash alternative to policy holders as part of its demutualisation, as did National Mutual Holdings Ltd, another Australian insurer seeking listing.

Smedley said Colonial would most likely seek to time its listing for after the announcement next year of either its 1996 annual or 1997 interim results. The group announced annual results in March this year.
He also ruled out having a prospectus sent out before the end of this year.
Colonial, which has funds under management in excess of A$36 billion, is expected to have a market capitalisation of US$1.5 billion on listing.
